actual_scope: Answer question 3 of PR6701 for complete common-image complement guards with finite-field row dependencies. Determine when a pencil of distinct directions passes jointly more or less often than its marginal independence prediction.
scope_change_reason: The original card asks for a changed physical supplier invoice. The live source instead asks for the new nonbinary prefix rule and orbit weights. The selected-baseline binding was checked; the changed scope is a theoretical side result.
bottleneck_link: A caller checking multiple directions on the same uniform header needs a joint probability. Marginals and even all pair probabilities can give the wrong side of the independence prediction. Conversion to a paid caller would require a named header producer, its selection/dispatch/restoration charges, and precise target credit.
stop_rule: Stop after deriving the fixed-image law and pencil signs, enforcing named masks, checking extension-field arithmetic against literal complete headers, and exporting a replay from source history.
evidence: PROOF.md, SIGN.md, TRIPLES.md and SMALL-FIELDS.md give the fixed-image law, all-dimension pencil signs, the independent-triple comparison and sharp field-order boundary. Finite evidence includes explicit matrix masks, all affine-plane subsets, two counts of the 17 exceptional triples and direct prefix counts for the five ternary quartets. Positive and negative controls are registered in VERIFY.json.
